items.text: Recap: operations in terms of algebras
$G\leftrightarrow A$, $X\leftrightarrow B$, $M$ a $k$-module:

\pi\colon A\to A\otimes A\ \ (\text{composition law}),\qquad \omega\colon B\to B\otimes A\ \ (\text{operation, an algebra homomorphism}),\qquad \delta_M\colon M\to M\otimes A\ \ (\text{operation on }M)
$G$ operating on $X$ (on the left) = $G$ operating on the right on the algebra $B$ of $X$, respecting the algebra structure.
From $\delta_M$ to the action of a point
$g\in G(k')$ is an algebra homomorphism $g\colon A\to k'$; the action on $M_{k'}$ is the $k'$-linear extension of
g_M^0=(1_M\otimes g)\circ\delta_M\colon M\to M\otimes A\to M\otimes k'
The two axioms
\text{(unit)}\qquad M\xrightarrow{\ \delta_M\ }M\otimes A\xrightarrow{\ 1\otimes\varepsilon\ }M\ =\ \mathrm{id}_M
\text{(associativity)}\qquad\begin{CD} M @>{\delta_M}>> M\otimes A\\ @V{\delta_M}VV @VV{1\otimes\pi}V\\ M\otimes A @>{\delta_M\otimes 1}>> M\otimes A\otimes A \end{CD}
Operation on the right ($g(g'x)=(g'g)x$): the same diagram followed by the symmetry of the last two factors. For monoids sides must be kept apart; formulas avoid $g^{-1}$.
Comodules

The operation depends only on the coalgebra structure of $A$ ($\pi$ associative, $\varepsilon$ unit). A left comodule over the coalgebra $A$: $\delta\colon M\to M\otimes A$ with the unit axiom and the associativity axiom.
Coalgebras via functors
Claim. A coalgebra structure on the $k$-module $A$ = an algebra structure on the module functor $V(A)\colon k'\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-lin}}(A,k')$ over $\mathcal O$.
$M$ is a left comodule over $A$ iff $V(M)$ is a right $V(A)$-module (compatibly with the $\mathcal O$-structure).
For $k$-modules $P,Q,R$:
\operatorname{Hom}_k(R,P\otimes Q)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O\text{-bilin}}\bigl(V(P)\times V(Q),V(R)\bigr)
(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto\Bigl(R\to P\otimes Q\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\otimes\beta\ }k'\otimes k'\xrightarrow{\ p\ }k'\Bigr),\qquad p(x\otimes y)=xy
With $P=Q=R=A$: a comultiplication $A\to A\otimes A$ = a bilinear law on $V(A)$; unitary = two-sided unit; associative = associative law.
$\delta\colon M\to M\otimes A$ = a pairing $V(M)\times V(A)\to V(M)$; the axioms say: unit acts as unit, associativity. So left comodule over $A$ = right module over the algebra functor $V(A)$.
The algebra of distributions
H=V(A)(k)=A^{\vee}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,k)\qquad(\text{algebra of distributions of the coalgebra }A)
$M$ left comodule $\Rightarrow$ $V(M)$ right $H$-module, $W(M)$ left $H$-module, hence $M$ a left $H$-module.
The module structure over $H$ alone does not in general reconstruct the comodule structure (one needs the operations of all $V(A)(k')$).
Action of $s\in H$ on $M$:
M\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }M\otimes A\xrightarrow{\ 1\otimes s\ }M\otimes k=M
Case 1: $A$ projective of finite type
\operatorname{Hom}_k(M,M\otimes A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M,\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,M))=\operatorname{Hom}_k(H\otimes M,M)
Then comodules over $A$ = left modules over $A^\vee$ (equivalent).
Case 2: $A$ a direct sum of projectives of finite type (e.g. $k$ a field)
A=\varinjlim A_\alpha,\quad H=\varprojlim A_\alpha^\vee\ \text{(surjective transitions)};\ \ H\ \text{has the inverse-limit topology (simple convergence)}
\operatorname{Hom}_k(N,M\otimes A)=\operatorname{Hom}^{\text{cont}}_k\bigl(H\otimes N,\,M\bigr)
Continuous: for each $x\in N$, $s\mapsto s\cdot x$ factors through some $A_\alpha^\vee$ ($M$ discrete).
A left comodule structure on $M$ = a left $H$-module structure with $s\mapsto s x$ continuous for every $x\in M$.
Coalgebra structure on $A$ in terms of $H$

$A$ a direct sum of projectives of finite type: a coalgebra structure on $A$ = a continuous bilinear product on $H=A^\vee$; unitary = two-sided unit $\varepsilon\in A^\vee$; associative = associative product. So a coalgebra = a topological algebra $H$.
R\to P\otimes Q\ \longmapsto\ P^\vee\times Q^\vee\to R^\vee\ \text{(continuous, bilinear)};\ \text{bijective when }P,Q,R\ \text{are direct sums of projectives of finite type}
